ATLAS HISTORICAL TERRITORY EDITIONS

Selectable Roman provinces, ca. AD 117:
Harvard Mapping Past Societies / Digital Atlas of Roman and Medieval Civilizations (DARMC).
Contributor: Matthew Polk. Source cited by DARMC: Talbert, Richard J. A. (ed.), Barrington Atlas of the Greek and Roman World (2000), Princeton.
Public source service: https://services1.arcgis.com/qN3V93cYGMKQCOxL/ArcGIS/rest/services/DARMC_Roman_World/FeatureServer/14

Selectable medieval realms, ca. AD 1200:
Harvard Mapping Past Societies / DARMC.
Contributors: Darryl Campbell, Nathaniel Donoghue, Kelly Gibson, Matthew Polk.
Public source service: https://services1.arcgis.com/qN3V93cYGMKQCOxL/ArcGIS/rest/services/DARMC_Medieval_World/FeatureServer/11

Source documentation: https://darmc.harvard.edu/map-sources
Source availability: https://darmc.harvard.edu/data-availability

Atlas groups matching source names for selection, rounds coordinates to five decimal places and supplies cartographic label anchors. Realm subdivisions may remain visible as internal lines. Papal States are separated from the source Holy Roman Empire grouping. Clearly later source entries (Golden Horde and Kingdom of Granada), and the already-lost Duchy of Edessa, are omitted from the ca. 1200 display. Source reconstructions are approximate; the medieval layer has broad generalisations and incomplete western North African coverage. This is an educational regional map, not a precise or exhaustive sovereignty survey.

Physical map detail: Natural Earth 1:50m coastlines and river/lake centre lines (public domain), https://www.naturalearthdata.com/ and https://github.com/nvkelso/natural-earth-vector/. Modern geography is included as an orientation aid; ancient river courses and shores could differ.

Original Roman extent reference, retained as roman-empire-117.geojson:
Ancient World Mapping Center, UNC Chapel Hill; Barrington Atlas and OpenStreetMap, ODbL 1.0. Source: https://github.com/AWMC/geodata/tree/master/Cultural-Data/political_shading/roman_empire_ce_117_extent
License: https://opendatacommons.org/licenses/odbl/1-0/

Retrieved October 31, 2026. Historical quiz results remain independent of modern country ranks.

Roman Republic, 60 BC: Ancient World Mapping Center (AWMC), Roman territory 60 BC; Barrington Atlas / AWMC modifications to OpenStreetMap. ODbL 1.0. Atlas groups source polygons into broad geographic regions; these are not exact provincial boundaries.
Source: https://github.com/AWMC/geodata/tree/master/Cultural-Data/political_shading/roman_empire_bce_60
Adapted database available in republic-territories.geojson under ODbL 1.0.

Muslim World during the Crusades, Mediterranean focus c. AD 1200: three dynastic regions selected from the same DARMC medieval source, with city points for orientation. Original polygons are incomplete in Morocco and Iberia; no additional boundaries have been invented. See historical.json for museum sources on the Ayyubids, Almohads and Seljuqs of Rum.
